explain.say: An octopus can vanish against rock, sand or seaweed in under a second. It starts by looking: its eyes take in how bright, patterned and rough the background is.

explain.say: Its brain picks a pattern and sends nerve signals straight to the skin. Thousands of tiny muscles pull on chromatophores, elastic sacs of red, yellow and brown pigment, stretching them wide.

explain.say: Below the pigment sacs, reflector cells bounce and scatter light, adding shimmer, whites and blues. Because muscles do the work, the change takes a fraction of a second.

faq.q: Why can an octopus change colour so fast?
faq.a: Its pigment sacs are opened by muscles controlled directly by nerves from the brain, not by slow hormones. A pattern can appear in a fraction of a second.
asks: How quickly can an octopus change colour?
Why is octopus camouflage faster than a chameleon's?

faq.a: Chromatophores are tiny elastic sacs of pigment in the skin, each ringed by little muscles. When the muscles pull, the sac stretches into a wide coloured dot; when they relax, it shrinks to a speck.

faq.q: How can an octopus look like a rock?
faq.a: It raises bumps of skin called papillae into knobs, spikes and ridges, and holds its arms in rock-like shapes, so its outline and texture vanish into the reef.
asks: Can an octopus change its skin texture?

faq.a: Surprisingly, most octopuses have only one kind of light sensor in their eyes, so they probably cannot see colour the way we do. How they still match colours so well is still being studied; their skin contains light-sensing proteins too.
The mimic octopus of Southeast Asia changes colour, pattern and body shape to imitate dangerous animals, such as lionfish, flatfish and sea snakes, to scare off predators.
asks: Can an octopus pretend to be another animal?

facts: Octopus chromatophores are pigment sacs opened by muscles under direct nerve control, which lets colour change in a fraction of a second.
Most octopuses have only one type of photoreceptor in their eyes, so they are thought to be colour blind.

quiz.say: What makes an octopus's colour change so fast?

options.show: Nerves control muscles around pigment sacs
options.say: Nerves control muscles around pigment sacs

quiz.why: Direct nerve signals make muscles stretch pigment sacs within a fraction of a second.

wrong.1: Octopuses do not shed skin to change colour.
wrong.2: Food colour does not cause quick changes; muscles do.
